episodes.177369: A series of severe thunderstorms produced large hail and strong, damaging winds during the overnight hours of March 27 as a cold front drifted southward toward the coastline.
episodes.177370: Strong thunderstorms developed along the coast as a cold front advanced southward on the evening of March 27, resulting in strong wind gusts observed around Galveston Bay.
episodes.177993: Strong thunderstorms ahead of a cold front moved through the area with a few measured gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.178336: A nearly stationary front draped itself from central Texas northeast through the Ohio River Valley and produced multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms, some with very heavy rainfall. Scattered showers and thunderstorms resulted in several cases of flooding or flash flooding. One to three inches of rain fell across the region with isolated higher amounts before the front passed east on the 25th. Moderate to heavy rainfall quickly inundated ditches and once again flooded roads around the region. Rivers throughout southern Illinois rose above flood stage. The river flooding was minor to moderate.
episodes.178338: A nearly stationary front draped itself from central Texas northeast through the Ohio River Valley and produced multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms, some with very heavy rainfall. Scattered showers and thunderstorms resulted in isolated flooding of roads. The rainfall pushed the Wabash. White, and Ohio Rivers above flood stage. The river flooding was mostly minor.
episodes.178339: A nearly stationary front draped itself from central Texas northeast through the Ohio River Valley and produced multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms, some with very heavy rainfall. Scattered showers and thunderstorms resulted in several cases of flooding or flash flooding. One to three inches of rain fell across the region with isolated higher amounts before the front passed east on the 25th. Moderate to heavy rainfall quickly inundated ditches and once again flooded roads around the region. Parts of the Ohio and Green Rivers rose above flood stage.
episodes.178406: A cold front and associated upper level low came through the Bay Area and Central Coast March 28 and 29. The front brought steady precipitation to the region, while the upper level low gave the area convective showers. Pea sized hail was reported across portions of the region.
episodes.178472: Lightning from snow showers struck near an oil battery.  The lightning strike damaged the oil battery and a trailer next to the oil tanks.
episodes.178662: A strong winter storm brought moderate to heavy rain with with flooding of roadways,  streams and creeks, with mudslides also reported. There was continued river flooding along the already elevated Sacramento, San Joaquin, Cosumnes, Mokelumne, and Tuolumne rivers. The storm brought dangerous mountain travel conditions with snow levels around down to 2000 feet, locally 1000 feet in Shasta County. Storm totals reached 1 to 3 feet of above 5000 feet. Winds gusted up to 35-50 mph in the Central Valley. In the mountains there were gusts up to 50 to 70 mph, which coupled with heavy snow, brought whiteout conditions. The were numerous road closures, including Interstate 80, Interstate 5 north of Fawndale, as well as State Routes 88, 89 and 299. Widespread trees down across the area blocked roads and caused power outages. There were thunderstorms on the 28th with a funnel cloud reported visible from the tower at Redding Airport.  There was a fatality reported when man was trapped by a collapsed snow bank next to his home.
episodes.178820: Severe thunderstorms developed across southwest Alabama and created several reports of large hail.
episodes.178890: A surface boundary associated with shortwave trough was draped across the CWA during the morning hours of March 28th. A few hours after midnight, stronger thunderstorms began to pop up along the boundary. One cell briefly turn severe as it moved into Southwest Mississippi, producing half dollar sized hail. This storm moved off to the northeast out of our CWA and no additional storms turned severe.
episodes.178931: Snowmelt during late March resulted in rises on some small streams and creeks across the region. Some of these rises pushed toward or into minor flood stage for a short period, but overall impacts were limited mainly to agricultural land.
episodes.178958: A prolonged, active weather pattern persisted across Georgia through late March, culminating in a series of disturbances that impacted the region March 25th through March 28th. In addition to numerous reports of damaging winds, hail and a few tornadoes, extreme rainfall amounts caused flash flooding over portions of the state. A swath of 4 or more inches of rain stretched from LaGrange, to Forsyth, to Augusta, with isolated amounts above 10 inches.
episodes.180931: A few stronger storms, buoyed by day time instability and adequate wind shear, developed across south Mississippi on the 28th of March. Mostly small hail was reported but some isolated stones as large as quarters was noted.

events.narrative: The public reported flooding at the intersection of Cook Road and Lower Big Springs Road. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 3 inches of rain fell over the area the day prior, with an additional 3 to 6 inches accumulating on March 27, resulting in the flash flooding.
Minor flooding occurred on the Ohio River. There was minor flooding of low-lying fields and woodlands.

A lightning strike from snow showers caused damage to an oil battery and a trailer next to the oil tanks.  The trailer was used for fracking.  Damage to the trailer included lights and tires being burned.  Three of the tanks were completely destroyed, while the fire in two others had burned out.
Video posted to social media showed estimated half dollar size hail in the Deer Park area.
Thunderstorm winds downed large tree limbs in a neighborhood in La Porte.
Strong thunderstorm winds knocked over several shipping containers at an industrial facility in Deer Park.
A member of the public measured golf ball sized hail in a residential area of Deer Park.
Images from a member of the public showed gold ball sized hail near Morgan's Point.
An MPING user reported quarter sized hail in La Porte.

The Emergency Manager relayed a report of a dam breach at Lake Tchukolako following a period of heavy rainfall. In the preceding 36-hours, the area of the lake and the immediate upstream basin received 3 to 5 inches of rain, causing the dam to be overwhelmed. Although the dam failed at approximately 1 AM EST March 28, it was being monitored for 'imminent failure' through the day March 27. The failure resulted in flooding and the subsequent closure of Wrigley Road. This dam had previously failed in May 2020, and repairs were complete in summer 2022.
A wind gust of 53 mph was observed at the State Hwy 87 WxFlow site.
A lightning strike ignited a fire in a church along FM 518 in League City, causing damage to the building.
Mostly pea to penny hail, but a few oblate shaped hail stones with a maximum diameter of 1 inch fell across the area.
Emergency management reported half dollar sized hail.
Minor flooding occurred on the Ohio River. There was minor flooding of low-lying woods and fields near the river. The river remained above flood stage into early April.

Willow Creek near Crooks rose above flood stage during the afternoon of March 28th before cresting around 0.51 feet above flood stage (9.51 feet) that evening. The creek then fell below flood stage during the late afternoon hours of March 29th.
Street flooding was reported on California Highway 92 in Spanishtown near Half Moon Bay. One way traffic controls were in effect as firefighters dealt with the flooding.
Redding Municipal Airport ASOS reported a brief funnel cloud.
Social media reported pea-sized hail near Van Ness Ave and Lombard St.
Roadway flooding was reported at the intersection of Blanco Road and Davis Road in Salinas.
